title: Calls 'just to talk', hidden suicide risk and overdose

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi. I don't know if this is the right number. It's not really an emergency.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I just can't sleep. I haven't slept properly in weeks. I just wanted to talk to someone, I guess.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: I hear you. Are you alone right now?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yeah. I gave my cat to my sister yesterday, so it's really quiet here now.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Why did you give your cat away?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: She'll take better care of him. It won't matter after tonight anyway.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: When you say it won't matter after tonight, are you thinking about killing yourself?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: ... I've sorted things out. I wrote some letters. Everyone would be better off, honestly.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Thank you for telling me. Have you done anything to hurt yourself today? Have you taken anything?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I took a few of my sleeping pills. Maybe more than a few. The whole strip I think.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: What's your address? I want to get help to you right now.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I don't know... Fjelievägen 7. Lund. Apartment 3.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: I'm sending an ambulance. Can you unlock your front door? And stay on the line with me.
